packageRules.description: Renovate's own config:recommended sets semanticCommitType through a packageRule, and packageRules beat top-level config. Setting it at the top level therefore does nothing at all: every upgrade stays chore and cuts no release.
Bazarr supports Python 3.13 and below, and says so on startup when it is given anything newer. It is the only application on base-python, so the ceiling can sit on the image itself.

Plex tags carry a per-build commit hash, and docker versioning treats everything after the first dash as a compatibility suffix it will not cross. Every release mints a fresh hash, so no newer tag is ever compatible and no update was ever offered. Parsing the four numeric parts and declaring no compatibility group is what lets the build number order the tags.

Bumping the application a container runs is what users see, so it has to reach them. release-please only cuts a release for fix and feat, and it attributes a commit to an application by the files that commit touches.
